summary: Ramon N. Prats is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources (attested 1999) and Pompeu Fabra University (attested 2017), and he taught Antonio Terrone.
Randall Studstill works in the fields of religious studies and philosophy. He studied under Steven D. Goodman and completed his doctoral studies under Richard Payne.

Randy J. LaPolla is a linguist and sinologist who studied at the University of California, Berkeley (1983–1990) under James A. Matisoff (~1985–1990). He served as professor at the City University of Hong Kong (~1996–2004) and joined Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai in 2021.

Rangama Chandawimala specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Kakkapalliya Anuruddha, also studying under Attaragama Gnanawimala. As of 2026, he is an associate professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (1924–1981) was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kalu Rinpoche, the 11th Tai Situpa, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and the 1st Beru Khyentse Rinpoche, teaching numerous prominent students.

Raniero Gnoli (1930–2025) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Mario Praz (~1948–1953) and Giuseppe Tucci (~1948–1954), later serving as Professor of Indology at Sapienza University of Rome from 1964 to 2000.
Ranu Kunwar is a PhD student at the Australian National University (attested 2026), studying under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron.
Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He served as a professor of Buddhist studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz (attested 2003 and 2017).
Raphael Kühner (1802–1878) was a linguist who studied at Ernestinum Gotha and the University of Göttingen (~1821–1825). He later taught Georg Bühler.

Raphael von Koeber (1848–1923) was a philosopher who studied at the Moscow Conservatory (~1867–1872), Heidelberg University (~1873–1874), and the University of Jena (~1874–1881). In 1893, he took up a post at the University of Tokyo.

Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh (1897–1982) was an Indologist and historian. He earned a BA at Fergusson College (~1914–1918) under Ramchandra Dattatrya Ranade, also studying under Sukhlal Sanghvi and Muni Jinavijaya. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and Ancient Indian History at Gujarat Vidyapith (~1920–1930).

Rasmus Rask (1787–1832) was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Odense Katedralskole and the University of Copenhagen, where he later held posts as librarian and professor of literary history (1825) and Eastern languages (1831).

Ratna Basu is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1989. She served as Professor (Special Invitee) at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Ratna Vajra Rinpoche (born 1974) is a scholar and practitioner in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, whom he succeeded in 2017.

Ravi M. Gupta is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Boise State University and the University of Oxford. He taught at Florida, Centre College, and William & Mary before becoming the Charles Redd Chair of Religious Studies at Utah State University (~2013).

Ravindra Singh Bisht is an archaeologist and Indologist educated at the University of Lucknow, ASI Institute of Archaeology, and Kumaun University. He worked for archaeology departments in Punjab and Haryana before serving as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (~1989–2004).

Rawi Bhavilai (1925–2017) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Chulalongkorn University, the University of Adelaide, and the Australian National University, serving as a physics professor (1945–1986) and director at Chulalongkorn University, and as a Royal Institute fellow (~1986–2017).

Raymond West (1832–1912) was an Indology scholar who studied under Martin Haug (~1860–1866). He served as a puisne judge at Bombay High Court (1873–1887), Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (~1883–1886), and Reader in Indian Law at Cambridge (~1895–1907).

Reb Anderson is a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher who studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Richard Baker, whom he succeeded. He served as abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center from ~1986 to 1995.
Rebecca Hufen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, she is a doctoral student under Dorji Wangchuck and a lector for Tibetan Studies at the University of Hamburg.
